To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cardiac biomarkers are sensitive indicators of cardiac late effects of anthraclyclines in childhood cancer survivors.

high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs cTnT), cardiac troponin I (cTtnI), and N‐terminal pro brain natriuretic Peptide (NT‐pro BNP) levels are elevated in long‐term childhood and young adult cancer survivors treated with anthracyclins, and that the presence of cardiac troponin autoantibodies is common among these patients.

high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T and troponin autoantibodies are associated with subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in long‐term childhood and young‐adult cancer survivors exposed to high‐doses of anthracycline chemotherapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cardiac troponins, natriuretic peptides and autoantibodies in the diagnosis and management of anthracycline cardiomyopathy.
the role of cardiac troponin and natriuretic peptides as biomarkers in the detection of cardiac toxicity among childhood cancer survivors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(1) cTnT, cTnI, NT‐proBNP, and high‐sensitivity troponin T are not useful as screening tools for cardiac late effects among childhood cancer survivors exposed anthracyclins; (2) NT‐proBNPs may be useful in predicting the presence of cardiac late effects among survivors with known cardiac late effects, but this requires confirmation in a prospective study.

the role of cardiac troponins in screening childhood cancer survivors for late effects of anthracyclines is not well understood and further studies are required to determine the role of cardiac imaging and cardiac biomarkers in screening for late cardiac effects of anthrachylines.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cardiac biomarkers NT‐proBNP and cTnT are elevated among long‐term survivors of childhood cancer who received anthracyclins, and that cTnAAbs are elevated among those who received radiation.
cardiac biomarkers are useful in identifying cardiac dysfunction in childhood cancer survivors exposed anthracyclins.
cardiac biomarkers are not useful for screening of late effects of anthraclyclines in long term childhood cancer survivors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of high‐sensitive cardiac biomarkers and troponin autoantibodies may improve the detection of cardiac late effects among childhood cancer survivors exposed long ago to anthracycline therapy.
cardiac biomarkers are useful in identifying childhood cancer survivors with cardiac late effects.

the use of cardiac biomarkers in childhood cancer survivorship may help identify individuals at increased risk for subclinical cardiac late effects, particularly those with a history of anthracycline exposure.
